symptom: DESCRIBE -> drop + create of a decision one of whose branches ends the flow (case / split type with a returning arm, if-elsif with a later returning branch) added an ExclusiveMerge: describe printed `end case; join shared1; merge shared1;`, the rebuild had the decision's merge plus the label's wired merge -> merge at one point, and each further round trip added `join junctionN; merge junctionN;`. create or modify (splice) was unaffected.
cause: labelCrossedMerges labels the Recombinable entry when it is not the split's post-dominator; with an arm that returns, the post-dominator is the exit, so the decision's OWN merge got a crossed label, and continueAfterSplitJoin printed `join L` after `end case`. The builder always draws the decision's merge when two arms fall through, then drew the join edge from it to the label's merge.
insight: Fixed in the builder, not the describer: `end X; join L;` is printed exactly when the split's own join is the labelled merge, so the builder can contract it - when the join leaves an unlabelled merge with no other way out and is the label's only way in - and that holds whatever reason the labeller had. Suppressing the label in describe instead would have had to re-derive each labeller's reason (sharedArmEntries labels the split's join on purpose). assertDescriptionRebuildsGraph contracts merges by design, so it is blind to this class: count merges and require a fixed point. The loop-body shape from the report (`if … then break; elsif … else … end if;`) did not reproduce on HEAD in three variants - not covered by the test.
